Not measured yet. To try it: enter a kid\'s profile, then press Home on the remote.
The goal: Shasha comes back within 2 seconds at most.

In the adult profile, the guard only steps in during a Serious Mode video or when time is up, and not after a kid\'s profile was left with the parent PIN until another profile is chosen. At those times, whoever reaches the TV\'s settings can stop the app, clear its data or uninstall it, revoke these two permissions, or bring YouTube back.
“Force stop” in settings stops the guard until the app is opened again, and restarting the TV doesn\'t bring it back.

In a kid\'s profile and in Serious Mode, the Home button, the remote\'s app buttons, voice commands, casting from a phone and the HDMI input aren\'t blocked: whatever appears is covered and Shasha comes back within a second or two.

This is a Fire TV, and Amazon doesn\'t officially support an app covering other apps. Try the guard once: enter a kid\'s profile and press Home. If Shasha doesn\'t come back by itself, the guard doesn\'t work on this device, and the lock inside the app stays as it is.
Blocking all of that needs ⁨Device Owner⁩ mode, which was ruled out on purpose: the lock isn\'t unbreakable.

In a kid\'s profile, when time is up and outside viewing hours, only the parent PIN leaves Shasha (on the TV, or switching profiles from the phone page with its own counter). If the PIN is locked after wrong attempts (5 minutes up to 4 hours; restarting doesn\'t end the wait) or forgotten, the whole TV stays on Shasha until the wait or the block ends. The way out: from the computer that set it up, with debugging still on, run ⁨%1$s⁩ (the guard stops until the app is opened again).
